country.name: Chile
country.languagePolicy: Spanish is the default interface language. Indigenous languages, Rapa Nui context and Chilean Sign Language require locally appropriate community, linguistic and institutional review; automatic translation is not reviewed localization.

review.policy: No category becomes verified without a named qualified Chilean reviewer, current authoritative sources and review of the responsible national, regional, local, community, institution or program authority.

governanceModel.summary: Chile combines MINEDUC policy, official recognition and school information with CNED normative and higher-education functions, the Superintendencia de Educación's oversight, SIES information and CNA accreditation decisions. Public education administration may involve Local Public Education Services, municipalities and other maintainers.
governanceModel.schoolRule: Preserve RBD, official name, region, commune, dependency or maintainer, teaching levels and types, current operating and recognition status, source date and review date.
governanceModel.higherEducationRule: Official recognition, institutional autonomy or licensing status, accreditation, a particular program's status and statistical indicators are distinct claims and require separate current evidence.

authorities.name: Ministerio de Educación
authorities.role: national policy, curriculum, official recognition and school information

authorities.name: Consejo Nacional de Educación
authorities.role: approval of curricular bases and functions concerning official recognition, licensing or closure in higher education as legally applicable

authorities.name: Superintendencia de Educación
authorities.role: oversight of the school education system and rights of educational communities

authorities.name: Centro de Estudios MINEDUC
authorities.role: official education datasets, statistics and research

authorities.name: Servicio de Información de Educación Superior
Comisión Nacional de Acreditación
authorities.role: institutional and applicable program accreditation decisions

authorities.name: Public and private school maintainers and Local Public Education Services
authorities.role: administration of schools within their legal competence

curriculum.authority: MINEDUC, with approval of applicable curricular bases by CNED
curriculum.title: Bases Curriculares, planes and programas de estudio currently in force
curriculum.implementationRule: Confirm level, modality, subject, governing decree, version, effective date, approved study plan or program, and the institution's educational project before mapping a resource.
curriculum.supplementPolicy: External materials may supplement but never silently replace the currently effective curricular bases, study plans, programs, institutional educational project or a community-governed intercultural curriculum.

schoolDirectory.scopeNotice: MIME supports search by RBD, region, commune, dependency, teaching level and other characteristics. A listing or displayed characteristic does not by itself prove current official recognition for every site, level, specialty, agreement or service.
requiredRecordFields: official recognition status and source when available

educationStatistics.authority: Centro de Estudios MINEDUC and applicable official statistical source
educationStatistics.scopeNotice: Every figure must display reference year, publication or update date, measure, population, geography, dependency, source and filters. Enrollment, establishment, performance and higher-education indicators must not be combined without labeling their datasets and periods.

higherEducation.recognitionAuthority: MINEDUC or law, with CNED functions as applicable
higherEducation.authorityNotice: Official recognition authorizes an institution to operate and award titles or degrees within its scope. Institutional autonomy or licensing status, CNA institutional accreditation, a particular undergraduate or postgraduate program's accreditation, and statistical indicators are distinct claims. Each must identify its decision, scope, date and effective period.

privacyAndSafeguarding.currentDataProtectionLaw: Ley N.º 19.628, current version through 30 November 2026
privacyAndSafeguarding.futureReform: Ley N.º 21.719 reforms enter into force on 1 December 2026; BRASA must not apply the deferred version as current before that date
privacyAndSafeguarding.childrenRightsLaw: Ley N.º 21.430 on guarantees and comprehensive protection of children's and adolescents' rights, plus other current safeguarding rules
privacyAndSafeguarding.scopeNotice: The applicable personal-data regime must be selected by effective date. Children's rights, consent or authorization, safeguarding, incident handling and institutional protocols require qualified Chilean review before real learner participation.

culturalAndLanguageRequirements.rule: Education affecting Indigenous peoples must respect current curricular rules, language and cultural context, participation and consultation requirements. A proposal under Indigenous consultation must not be presented as an approved curriculum. BRASA must not substitute automatic translation for community participation.

completionCriteria: A qualified Chilean education reviewer is named.
MINEDUC, CNED, Superintendencia, maintainer and local public education responsibilities are reviewed for the participating institution.
Every school record preserves RBD, dependency or maintainer, levels, specialties, status, recognition evidence, source date and review date.
Every statistic shows reference year, update date, definition, geography, population and provenance.
Every higher-education claim distinguishes official recognition, autonomy or licensing, institutional accreditation, program accreditation and statistical indicators.
Curriculum mappings identify level, modality, subject, decree, version, effective date, approved plan or program and institutional project.
Indigenous language and cultural requirements are reviewed with competent community participation, and proposals under consultation are not presented as approved.
The transition from Law 19.628 to Law 21.719 on 1 December 2026 and current child-protection requirements are reviewed by qualified Chilean counsel.
Privacy, safeguarding, accessibility, incident and consent procedures are approved by each participating institution.
No authorization, recognition, accreditation, partnership or credential claim exceeds documentary evidence.
